item.title: WiseTech Raided by Australia Antitrust Watchdog; Stock Sinks
item.description: WiseTech Global Ltd. said Australian antitrust authorities demanded the company hand over documents and data as part of an investigation into alleged breaches of competition law. The company’s stock tumbled.

item.title: NSE Eyes $55 Billion Valuation in IPO While Rival BSE’s Shares Lose Favor
item.description: The IPO is expected to launch in the second half of September.

item.title: China Recovers Rocket on Land in Push to Catch Up With SpaceX
item.description: China said it recovered a rocket booster on land for the first time, a major step toward catching up with US firms like Elon Musk’s SpaceX.

item.title: Oasis Urges Kakaku.com to Withdraw Support for EQT’s Buyout Bid
item.description: Kakaku.com Inc. shareholder Oasis Management Co. has asked the company to withdraw its support for EQT AB’s buyout bid on grounds that the offer is too low, escalating a bidding war for the Japanese price comparison site.

item.title: Australia Wage Growth Stays Elevated, Reinforces Price Pressures
item.description: Australia’s wage growth remained elevated, highlighting persistent price pressures in the economy at a time when the Reserve Bank is warning it’s willing to tighten further to restrain inflation.

item.title: PHP/USD: Philippine Peso Fell to New Record Low as Oil Prices Rise
item.description: The Philippine peso fell to a record low against the dollar as higher oil prices put renewed pressure on the currency.

item.title: AI Startup Temporal in Talks for a Valuation of at Least $12 Billion
item.description: Temporal Technologies Inc. is in talks for a fresh funding round that would give the AI startup a valuation of at least $12 billion before the new money, according to people familiar with the efforts.

item.title: Japan Bond Volatility Is Pumping Up Futures Trading in Singapore
item.description: Global funds and relative-value traders are driving a surge in Japan bond futures trading in Singapore, drawn by rising volatility.

item.title: Hitachi Construction Shares Drop After $740 Million Block Trade
item.description: Hitachi Construction Machinery Co.’s shares fell the most in almost three weeks after its major shareholder Hitachi Ltd. offloaded all holding, in the latest move by the Japanese conglomerate to divest some of its assets to focus on core businesses.

item.title: Evergrande Liquidators Challenge Hong Kong Watchdog in Court
item.description: A Hong Kong court is set to hear arguments on whether a deal that set up a fund to compensate China Evergrande minority shareholders is valid.

item.title: Australian Housing Shares Surge as Earnings Defy Property Slump
item.description: Shares of two of Australia’s largest property developers surged after stronger full-year earnings showed resilience in the face of a housing market downturn.

item.title: Korean Stocks Bear Brunt of Chip Selloff on Higher Yield Worry
item.description: South Korea led a selloff in Asian chip stocks, as rising bond yields exacerbated worry over the large sums of cash being shelled out by Big Tech.

item.title: Japanese Stocks Slide as Bond Market Anxiety Hits AI Sentiment
item.description: Japan’s Nikkei Stock Average slumped for a second day, weighed down by chip-related stocks as anxiety over surging bond yields sapped risk appetite from the AI trade.

item.title: Cerebras (CBRS) Says Its New Computer Boosts AI Speed Advantage Over Nvidia
item.description: Cerebras Systems Inc. introduced a new speedier computer built with the company’s chips, saying the device will give it a wider advantage over Nvidia Corp. equipment.

item.title: Indonesia Seen Holding Rates as New Chief Leads First Decision
item.description: Indonesia’s central bank is expected to hold rates in the first policy meeting led by Acting Governor Destry Damayanti, with investors paying close attention to how she’ll balance currency stability with the President Prabowo Subianto’s growth push.

item.title: Gold Holds Losses as Bond Selloff, Hormuz Limbo Weigh on Outlook
item.description: Gold steadied after the biggest drop in almost a month as a bond rout and deadlock in the Strait of Hormuz dimmed the outlook for the precious metal.

item.title: Terton Opposes Korea’s Golfzon on Second Buyout Bid
item.description: A second attempt to take South Korea’s Golfzon Holdings Co. private is facing renewed resistance from a minority shareholder, with the stock now trading above the tender price in a sign the buyer may struggle to win over investors on the current terms.

item.title: JBS Seeks Rest of Pilgrim’s Pride Stake in $1.2 Billion Deal
item.description: Pilgrim’s Pride Corp. shares jumped after meatpacking giant JBS NV offered to acquire the shares of the chicken producer it doesn’t already own in a stock deal valued at about $1.2 billion.

item.title: China’s Flatter Bond Curve Shows Deeper Policy Divide With Peers
item.description: A relentless drop in China’s long-end yields is driving an aggressive curve flattening, laying bare a stark macro rift with global markets where long-dated rates have hit multi-year peaks.

item.title: Hong Kong Exchanges’ Non-Equity Push Seen as Key for Stock Boost
item.description: With record trading volumes and new listings providing little boost for shares of Hong Kong Exchanges & Clearing Ltd., analysts are increasingly looking for a jolt from the company’s expansion of non-equity business.

item.title: Unitree Robotics Set to Debut After $904 Million Shanghai IPO
item.description: Unitree Robotics is set to begin trading in Shanghai Wednesday after raising 6.1 billion yuan ($904 million) in an initial public offering that will make it the first publicly traded humanoid robot maker in mainland China.

item.title: AI Boom and Energy Shocks See Growth in Southeast Asia Bifurcate
item.description: Vietnam retained its crown as Southeast Asia’s fastest-growing major economy in the second quarter, with Thailand the laggard, as tech and energy dictated varied fortunes across the region.

item.title: Japan’s Earnings Surprise Analysts to Fuel Bets for Broad Rally
item.description: Japanese companies posted their largest earnings beat in five years despite soaring oil costs, fueling hopes that strong profit growth across sectors can broaden the market rally beyond AI-related trades.

item.title: Chip Rout Clouds Asia Open as Bond Jitters Linger: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks in Asia were set to fall Wednesday after a selloff in US technology shares, as elevated bond yields, rising oil prices and renewed Middle East tensions prompted investors to pare risk.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 19
item.description: Oil rose for a fourth day, with no sign of progress toward a resolution of the US-Iran war after almost six months of conflict.

item.title: Fletcher Building Waiting on Meaningful Recovery in NZ Demand
item.description: New Zealand’s largest construction materials company Fletcher Building Ltd. doesn’t expect a meaningful recovery in its markets until 2027, adding to signs of muted economic growth over the second half of this year.

item.title: Uruguay Holds Interest Rates Steady With Inflation Below Target
item.description: Uruguay’s central bank held interest rates steady for a fourth consecutive policy meeting with inflation below its target.

item.title: Mizuho Markets Head Expects BOJ to Raise Rates Soon, More Often
item.description: Mizuho Financial Group Inc. expects the Bank of Japan to pick up the pace of interest-rate hikes, with the next one coming as soon as next month, as the weak yen and inflation prompt the central bank to act more quickly.

item.title: Anthropic Plans to Give CEO Extra Voting Power, Information Says
item.description: Anthropic PBC plans to give Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei and other co-founders shares with extra voting power as the firm prepares to make its Wall Street debut, The Information reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Bond Traders Are Hedging Risk Fed Pivots to Rate Cuts in 2027
item.description: Bond traders are changing gears again. After a raft of data helped all but price out interest rate hikes for the rest of the year, wagers in the options market are looking to hedge the risk that the Federal Reserve pivots to cutting rates in 2027.
